transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore. It's really noticeable, especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and handle paperwork or shared household plans. 

Like, my husband and I were trying to sit down at the kitchen table on Tuesday to go over the budget and the contractor quotes for our patio. We're thinking of putting in a fire pit, which I’m so excited about because I found these gorgeous Adirondack chairs on sale online. They're usually like three hundred dollars each, but I got them for half that. Shipping was a total nightmare, though. The delivery guy left them at the neighbor's house and I had to drag these huge boxes across the lawn in the rain, and our neighbor's dog kept barking at me the whole time. It's a Golden Retriever, super sweet usually, but he just hates boxes for some reason. 

But anyway... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, sitting at the table. Yeah, whenever we try to do those plans or I have to look at the paperwork, I just... I can't stay in the chair. I just feel totally restless.
When you're feeling restless like that, are you usually worrying about something specific?

No, not really. It's not like a worry or an anxiety thing, it's just... physical, you know? Like my legs just need to move. It's funny because my mom used to say I had "ants in my pants" when I was a kid. She actually used to make me go run laps around our cul-de-sac before dinner just so I'd sit still through the meal. We had this neighbor, Mr. Henderson, who was always out working on his lawn—he had the greenest grass on the block, seriously, it was like a golf course—and he'd always wave at me while I was running. He used to grow these amazing tomatoes, too. He gave us a basket once and my mom made this incredible homemade salsa. I tried to recreate the recipe last summer, but I couldn't get the spice level right. I think I used too many jalapeños, because my husband took one bite and his face turned bright red. We ended up having to order pizza instead. We always get it from that place downtown, the one with the really good garlic knots. 

But yeah, um, no, it's not worry. I just can't sit still.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks or pay attention to what you're doing when you're feeling restless?

Yeah, definitely. It's like... I can sit down with an email about the patio plans, or even just a chapter of a book I actually want to read, and I'll start out totally fine. But then, maybe five minutes later, I'm just staring at the exact same paragraph over and over, and I realize absolutely none of it went in. 

I was trying to read this historical fiction novel last week—it's set in 1920s Paris, which I've always wanted to visit. My sister went there for her honeymoon and she brought me back this beautiful silk scarf. It has these little Eiffel Towers woven into the pattern, but they're so subtle you can't even tell unless you look really closely. I wore it to a PTA meeting once and this other mom, Sarah, spilled her entire coffee on it. I was so upset, but I managed to get the stain out with this weird trick I found on Pinterest using club soda and white vinegar. Pinterest is so dangerous though, I can spend hours just looking at kitchen organization hacks. I bought all these clear plastic bins for my pantry, but I haven't actually put anything in them yet. They're just sitting in a stack on the dining room floor. 

So yeah, um, my focus just kind of evaporates. I'll read the same sentence five times and have no idea what it said.
Do you feel this restlessness at work or in other places besides home?

Yeah, it's pretty much everywhere, not just at home. Like, I don't work right now, but whenever I'm in church meetings or even just sitting at family dinners, I'm always doing something. I'll be twisting my wedding ring around and around, or bouncing my foot under the table, or just constantly shifting in my chair, even when I'm really trying hard to look composed and put together. 

My mother-in-law is always at those family dinners, and she has this way of looking at you when you're not sitting perfectly still. She’s very proper, you know? She used to be a ballet dancer when she was younger, so she has this incredible posture. She actually tried to teach my daughter some ballet positions in the living room last Thanksgiving, which was adorable, but then the turkey almost burned because we all got so distracted watching them. We had to order all these extra sides from a catering place at the last minute just in case the turkey was ruined. The catering place makes these amazing sweet potato biscuits, though. I actually asked for the recipe once, but they wouldn't give it to me. They said it was a family secret. I totally get that, my grandmother had a secret recipe for pecan pie that she took to her grave. I still dream about that pie. 

But um, yeah, I'm always fidgeting or bouncing my leg, no matter where I am.
Did you experience this restlessness when you were a child?

Oh, absolutely. Looking back, this was already a huge part of me way back in elementary school. I was always that girl with the incredibly messy desk, constantly losing my permission slips. My mom was always getting notes from my teachers saying I talked out of turn or just seemed completely unable to stay seated. 

Actually, speaking of permission slips, I remember this one time I forgot the slip for our fourth-grade field trip to the natural history museum, and I was so devastated because they had this huge new dinosaur exhibit. My daughter actually just went to a museum like that last month with her scout troop. She bought this little mood ring from the gift shop. Do you remember mood rings? Mine always used to turn black, which I think meant "stressed" or maybe "tired." Anyway, she dropped her ring in the car on the way home, and we spent like an hour tearing the backseat apart looking for it. We didn't find the ring, but we found so many petrified french fries under the floor mats. It was so gross. I really need to get my SUV detailed. There's this place by the grocery store that does the interior for a really good price, and they give you a free air freshener. I always pick the pine scent because it reminds me of Christmas, even if it's the middle of July. Christmas is going to be so crazy this year anyway because my brother is flying in from Seattle, and he's bringing his two golden retrievers. They shed absolutely everywhere, which is why I bought this special vacuum attachment online, but it doesn't work on the couch cushions at all. 

But um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, the teachers were always telling me to sit down and be quiet.
Do you usually feel restless when you're upset or angry about something?

Um, I don't think so? I mean, I'm not really sure if it's tied to being upset or angry. It's just kind of... always there. Like, I don't need to be mad to feel like I need to move. 

Though, speaking of being upset, I was pretty annoyed yesterday when I went to the post office. I had to mail this package to my sister—it was a belated birthday gift, just this really cute ceramic mug I found at a craft fair. The woman who made it said she uses a special kind of glaze that makes it safe for the dishwasher, which is so rare for handmade stuff, right? Anyway, the line at the post office was practically out the door. There was this guy in front of me who was arguing with the clerk about the price of stamps. He just kept going on and on about how they used to be so much cheaper. Which, I mean, he's not wrong, but it's not like the clerk can do anything about it. I ended up standing there for like twenty minutes, and my foot was just tapping the whole time. I almost left and went to one of those private shipping places, but they always charge you extra for the tracking number. I always need a tracking number because once I ordered this really expensive face serum online and it just completely vanished in transit. The company wouldn't refund me because they said it was delivered, but I swear it never showed up. It was supposed to have vitamin C and hyaluronic acid in it. I've been trying to get better about my skincare routine since I turned forty, but it's so hard to remember to do all the steps every single night. 

So, yeah, I don't think the restlessness is really about being mad. It just happens regardless of how I'm feeling.
Do you ever avoid certain activities or situations because of this restlessness?

I don't think I avoid anything because of it. I mean, I know I'm going to be fidgeting, but I still go. Like, I still go to the movies even though I'm shifting around in the seat the whole time. 

Actually, my husband and I just went to see a movie last weekend. The seats at our local theater recline now, which is nice, but the buttons to make them go up and down are so incredibly sensitive. I accidentally bumped it with my elbow and spilled half my popcorn. And theater popcorn is so ridiculously expensive now! We usually try to sneak in our own candy in my purse, like those little boxes of Milk Duds. My daughter loves Milk Duds, but she got braces last month, so she's not supposed to eat anything sticky or chewy. The orthodontist was very strict about it. He has this huge aquarium in his waiting room with these beautiful saltwater fish. I could watch them for hours, it's so relaxing. I actually thought about getting a fish tank for our living room, but I read online that saltwater tanks are a ton of work to keep the pH balanced and everything. I can barely keep my houseplants alive, let alone a bunch of tropical fish. I bought a fiddle leaf fig tree at the hardware store because they look so good in magazines, but all the leaves turned brown and fell off within a month. I think I overwatered it. Or maybe it didn't get enough light, since the big window in our living room faces north, so it's always kind of shadowy in there. 

But um... no, I don't really skip out on activities just because I can't sit still. I just kind of power through it, you know?
Do you notice that your restlessness tends to happen at specific times of the day?

Specific times? Um, no, I don't think so. It's not like it only happens in the morning or at night. It's just sort of... constant, I guess? 

Although, mornings are always so chaotic at our house anyway. Getting my daughter ready for school is like herding cats. She has this new routine where she insists on picking out her own outfits, which is fine, but yesterday she wanted to wear a tutu over her sweatpants. And she couldn't find her left shoe. We have this big basket by the front door where all the shoes are supposed to go, but somehow it always just ends up full of junk mail and dog leashes. We don't even have a dog anymore, but I keep the leashes just in case we ever decide to foster one. I follow this rescue group on Facebook that saves greyhounds from racing tracks, and they're always posting these heartbreaking pictures. They say greyhounds are actually huge couch potatoes, which you wouldn't expect because they run so fast. I tried taking up running a few years ago when I got my Fitbit. I even bought those really expensive Brooks sneakers that they map to your arch type at the running store. The guy had me jog on a treadmill while he recorded my feet with an iPad. But honestly, I hated it. Running just makes my lungs burn, and the sneakers ended up getting ruined anyway when I wore them to a music festival and it poured rain the entire weekend. We had to park in this muddy field, and my husband's car got stuck. We had to pay a guy in a pickup truck fifty bucks to tow us out. 

But, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, time of day. Yeah, no, I haven't really noticed it being worse at any particular time. It's pretty much an all-day thing.
Do you feel like your restlessness is ever triggered by feeling overwhelmed?

Um, overwhelmed? Yeah, I guess so. Actually, that's kind of what brings me in... I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore, you know? Especially when I have to sit down and do something quiet, like filling out paperwork or going over the household budget with my husband. 

We use this app for our budget, but I honestly hate it because the categories never make sense. Like, where are you supposed to put the money you spend on birthday gifts? Does that go under 'entertainment' or 'miscellaneous'? Last month I bought my niece this adorable little dollhouse for her fifth birthday. It was made of real wood, not that cheap plastic stuff, and it had all these tiny little furniture pieces. The couch even had real fabric on it. My sister said it took her three hours to put it together because the instructions were just pictures with no words. I hate when companies do that. It's like building IKEA furniture. We bought a dresser from IKEA once for the guest room, and it sat in boxes on the floor for a solid month before we finally tackled it. And then we realized we put the drawer tracks on backward. The guest room is mostly just storage right now anyway. I really want to paint it a nice sage green, but picking out paint colors is so stressful. You bring home those little paper swatches, and they look completely different on the wall than they do in the store under those fluorescent lights. 

But yeah, when I'm trying to focus on stuff like that, the paperwork or the planning, the restless feeling is just... it's really bad. I just can't settle down.
Do you think your restlessness might be related to feeling anxious?

Anxious? I mean, I guess I get anxious sometimes, but I don't think it's what makes me restless. I feel like I'm just always sort of buzzing, even when I'm perfectly happy. 

Like, I was at the grocery store the other day, totally fine, just looking for this specific type of artisanal cheese my husband likes. It's this smoked gouda that comes in a black wax rind. The deli counter guy was taking forever slicing turkey for the woman in front of me, and she wanted it shaved so thin it was practically see-through. I don't understand why people want their lunch meat that thin, it just falls apart when you try to make a sandwich. I tried making these pinwheel sandwiches for a PTA potluck once using really thin ham, and it was a total disaster. They just turned into mushy little blobs. I ended up throwing them away and buying a veggie tray from the store on the way to the school. Veggie trays are such a rip-off, though, right? You pay twenty dollars for a few carrots, some celery, and a tub of ranch dressing that tastes weirdly sweet. I usually make my own ranch dip using that hidden valley packet and sour cream, it's so much better. My daughter will actually eat broccoli if she can dip it in that. We've been trying to get her to eat more vegetables, but she's in this phase where she only wants foods that are beige. Chicken nuggets, french fries, plain pasta... it's exhausting. 

But um, no, I don't think it's anxiety. I'm not really worrying about anything when I can't sit still, I just physically have to keep moving.
Is your restlessness something that you experience all the time, or are there times when it goes away completely?

Um, goes away completely? I don't really think it ever completely stops. Even when I'm just at home for the day, I'm always doing something. Like, I'll start a load of laundry, and then on the way back to the living room I'll remember I need to check my emails, and while I'm doing that I'll notice the junk drawer is a mess so I start reorganizing that, and then I have to check the calendar... it's just this constant motion. I never really take a break. It feels like I'm being pushed from the inside to just keep moving. 

Speaking of that junk drawer, I found these old batteries in there yesterday and I have no idea if they're good or not. Do you know if there's a way to test them without one of those little battery tester things? My dad used to have this trick where he'd drop them on the table, and if they bounced a certain way it meant they were dead. Or maybe it meant they were good? I can't remember. He always had these weird little tricks for everything. He could fix anything with duct tape and WD-40. He used to have this old Ford pickup truck that he kept running for like twenty years just by tinkering with it on the weekends. It was this awful mustard yellow color, but he loved it. He finally sold it to a guy down the street who wanted to restore it, but I think it just sat in his driveway rusting for another five years. People always have these big plans for projects and then they just never follow through, you know? Like my husband's plan to build a deck in the backyard. We bought all the lumber last spring, and it's still just sitting under a tarp next to the garage. The tarp is starting to get all moldy, too. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, taking a break. Yeah, I don't really do that. I just kind of bounce from one thing to the next all day long.
Did you have trouble sitting still before you were 7 years old?

Before I was seven? Yeah, definitely. Looking back, this was already just... part of who I was in elementary school. I was always the girl with the completely messy desk. Like, you know those old wooden desks where you lift the top up? Mine was a disaster zone of crumpled papers and broken crayons. I used to love those big boxes of Crayola crayons, the ones with the sharpener built into the back? Though the sharpener never really worked, it just kind of chewed up the wax. And then the wax would get stuck inside and you'd have to dig it out with a paperclip. I used to make these little wax balls out of the shavings. 

But anyway, because my desk was such a mess, I was always forgetting my permission slips, too. I almost missed out on this one field trip to the planetarium because I left the slip on the kitchen counter. My mom had to drive all the way to the school to drop it off, and she was so mad because she had already bought me a special lunch for it—those little Lunchables with the crackers and the cheese? The pizza ones were always my favorite, though the sauce tasted a little like cold ketchup. I still buy them for my daughter sometimes when I don't feel like making a real lunch, even though they're probably terrible for you and the packaging is so bad for the environment. I try to recycle, but our city's recycling program is so confusing. Half the time they don't even pick up the bin if the lid isn't shut completely tight. 

But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, school. Yeah, my mom would get these notes from my teachers all the time saying I talked out of turn or just seemed completely unable to stay seated during lessons. My second-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she wore this incredibly strong floral perfume, like roses and baby powder mixed together, and she would always come stand right behind my chair to try and keep me in it. It gave me such a headache. But yeah, I've basically always been like this, even back then.
How old were you when you first noticed you had trouble sitting still or focusing on things?

Well, kind of like I was just saying, it was definitely back in elementary school. I guess I would have been around six or seven? First grade, maybe? That's when I really remember being the girl with the completely messy desk and always having those forgotten permission slips. 

First grade was also when we started getting to go to the big school library. The librarian, Mr. Henderson, he always wore these crazy bowties. He had this one that actually lit up, which I thought was the coolest thing ever. I have no idea where you even buy a light-up bowtie. Maybe one of those novelty shops at the mall? I haven't been to our local mall in forever. It's practically a ghost town now, half the stores are empty, and they turned the old Sears into this indoor mini-golf place. My husband took our daughter there for her birthday last month and said the green turf was already peeling up on the windmills. It's kind of sad how malls are just dying out, you know? I used to love going to the food court on weekends and getting an Orange Julius. Do they even make those anymore? I tried to make a smoothie at home last week that tasted like it, but I put way too much vanilla extract in and it was just awful. I had to pour the whole blender down the sink.

But um, wait, how old was I? Right, six or seven. Like I mentioned a minute ago, that's when my teachers started sending all those notes home to my mom complaining that I was talking out of turn or that I just couldn't stay seated during the lessons. So yeah, it's been there pretty much as long as I can remember.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for ADHD?

Um, no, I've never been officially diagnosed with anything like that, or, you know, given any medication for it. Honestly, I haven't really been to the doctor much at all lately, except for just regular checkups. My primary care doctor, Dr. Evans, he actually just retired last month. He was so great, he always remembered that I love gardening. Though my garden is an absolute disaster right now. The deer keep eating my hostas. I tried spraying that peppermint oil stuff on the leaves to keep them away, but it smells so strong, and I swear it just attracts the neighborhood cats instead. There's this one big orange tabby that just sleeps right in the middle of my flowerbed now. He completely squashed all my petunias. 

I think he belongs to the family down the street, the ones who put up their Christmas lights in October. I mean, I love Christmas, but October is just way too early, don't you think? We usually wait until at least Thanksgiving weekend. We get a real tree every year from this little farm out on Route 9. The pine needles get everywhere, though, and the vacuum always gets clogged. I had to take apart the whole vacuum cleaner last time because a twig got jammed in the roller brush. Have you ever tried taking apart a Dyson? It's like a puzzle. I spent like two hours watching YouTube tutorials just to figure out how to snap the plastic casing back together. 

But, um, wait, what was the question? Oh, right, treatment. No, no one's ever treated me for it or anything. This is really the first time I'm looking into it.
Do you feel like your restlessness is interfering with your ability to complete tasks or achieve your goals?

Yeah, it definitely is. I mean, the fallout has been that people at home and in my volunteer circles just... they can't reliably count on me anymore. I actually had to step back from some responsibilities recently because I keep letting things fall through, even though I'm really trying hard. Like, I was supposed to be in charge of the bake sale for the PTA last month. I had this whole spreadsheet set up and everything, color-coded by what kind of baked goods people were bringing. I love color-coding things. I bought these amazing pastel highlighters from Target, the ones that don't bleed through the paper? Though I ended up using them to color in this adult coloring book I bought instead of finishing the spreadsheet. Have you tried those coloring books? They're supposed to be so relaxing, but some of the patterns are just so tiny, you have to sharpen your colored pencils constantly. 

And then the pencil sharpener I have is one of those electric ones, and it makes this horrible grinding noise. It scares my dog every time I use it. He's a rescue, a terrier mix, and he's terrified of loud noises. We had to get him a Thundershirt for the Fourth of July because the fireworks in our neighborhood are just out of control. Our next-door neighbor, Gary, he sets off these massive ones that shake our windows. I swear it sounds like a war zone. I tried talking to his wife about it, but she just gave me this recipe for zucchini bread and changed the subject. The bread was actually really dry, too. I think she left it in the oven too long. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right, the bake sale. Yeah, I completely forgot to send out the reminder email to the volunteers, so half the people didn't show up with their stuff, and we barely raised any money. It was so embarrassing. So yeah, I've had to step back from things like that because I just can't seem to keep it all together, no matter how hard I try.
Have you ever noticed any significant improvement in your ability to focus or sit still when you're doing something you really enjoy or find very interesting?

Um, I don't know, maybe? I mean, I guess if I'm really, really into a book or something, I might not notice the time passing, but I don't know if that means I'm sitting still. I actually just started reading this new mystery novel. It's set in this little coastal town in Maine, and the descriptions of the ocean are just beautiful. I've always wanted to go to Maine. My aunt went there for her honeymoon, like, thirty years ago, and she brought me back this little snow globe with a lighthouse inside. I used to keep it on my nightstand, but it fell off and broke when I was trying to reach for my phone in the dark. 

My phone charger cord is just a little too short, you know? I need to buy one of those extra-long braided ones, but there are so many options on Amazon, I just get overwhelmed reading the reviews. Some people say they stop working after a week, and I don't want to waste ten dollars. Ten dollars could buy, like, two fancy coffees at that new cafe downtown. The one with the exposed brick walls? They make this lavender latte that is just amazing, but the parking down there is a nightmare. You have to parallel park on this really steep hill, and I always feel like I'm going to roll backward into the car behind me. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Focus? Yeah, I don't really know if I have an easier time focusing on fun stuff. I just feel kind of all over the place all the time, honestly.
Did you often have difficulty playing quietly or engaging in leisure activities as a child?

I mean, yeah, I've always struggled with that. Even now, honestly. Like, sometimes I just want to have a nice, quiet evening, you know? Just reading beside my husband on the couch. But I always end up talking, or humming some song that's stuck in my head, or getting up to grab a glass of water, or fixing a pillow, or just... making enough noise that it stops being peaceful. 

My husband is so patient, though. He usually just puts his headphones on. He has those really nice noise-canceling ones, the Bose ones? I bought them for him for our anniversary last year. We went to this Italian restaurant to celebrate, and the pasta was incredible, but the waiter kept hovering, which was kind of annoying. I hate when they ask how the food is right when you have a huge bite in your mouth. And then the table next to us was so loud, I think it was a bachelorette party or something. They had these little plastic tiaras. I wore a tiara for my wedding, actually, but it was real crystals, not plastic. It kept snagging in my veil, though. My hairdresser used, like, fifty bobby pins to keep it in place, and I had a headache for two days afterward. 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, playing quietly. Yeah, no, quiet just isn't really my thing, I guess. I just can't seem to settle down like that.
Do you think your restlessness and difficulty focusing are more related to inattention or hyperactivity?

I honestly don't know. I'm not really sure how to tell the difference between the two, to be honest. I actually tried looking that up on my iPad the other day to see if I could figure it out, but my iPad screen has this huge crack right down the middle. I dropped it in the driveway last week because I was trying to carry all the groceries inside in one trip. I absolutely refuse to make two trips. We use those heavy canvas bags from Trader Joe's, you know? Have you seen those little mini tote bags they came out with recently? People were literally fighting over them in the stores. My niece showed me a video of it on her phone. She's sixteen and she just got her learner's permit, which is terrifying. My sister let me ride in the back seat with them last weekend, and I swear I was pressing my foot on an imaginary brake pedal the entire time. She almost hit a mailbox. It was one of those really fancy brick mailboxes, too, the ones that look like a miniature house? If she had hit that, it would have completely totaled my sister's Honda. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking? Inattention or hyperactivity? Yeah, I really don't know. They just kind of feel like a big blur to me, so I couldn't really say if one is the main issue over the other.
Do you find that your mind often wanders off or that you have trouble following through on instructions, rather than feeling an intense need to be physically active?

Yeah, definitely. Following through is... it's a real struggle. Like, if my husband asks me to handle a few things in order, you know? Like, "Can you call the plumber, update the calendar, and send that form?" I'll do the first part, I'll call the plumber, but then I'll just drift into something else before the rest is finished. 

Speaking of the plumber, he came over last week to fix the sink in the guest bathroom. It had been dripping for months, just this constant *drip, drip, drip*. It was driving me insane. But he was this really nice older guy, and he brought his dog with him! He just left him in the truck, but I went out and pet him. It was a golden retriever mix, I think. I love golden retrievers. We had one growing up named Buster, and he used to steal my dad's socks and hide them under the sofa. My dad would get so mad because he only wore those really specific wool socks from L.L. Bean. They're super warm, though. I should probably buy a pair before winter hits. The winters here have been getting so cold lately. Last year, our heating bill was absolutely ridiculous. I tried to tell my husband we need to weather-strip the windows, but... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, following through. Yeah, I definitely have a hard time finishing a list of things. I just get sidetracked so easily.
Do you think you have more trouble with sitting still and fidgeting, or with paying attention and following through on tasks?

I mean, I think the fidgeting is probably worse? Or at least, it's more obvious to other people. Like, even when I'm trying really, really hard to look composed, I just can't stop moving. If we're at a family dinner or, like, a church meeting, I'm always twisting my wedding ring around my finger, or my foot is just bouncing under the table, or I'm shifting in my chair. 

Speaking of my wedding ring, I actually need to get it resized. My knuckles have gotten kind of swollen lately, I don't know why. Maybe I'm eating too much salt? I did buy those sea salt caramel pretzels from Costco last week, the ones in the huge tub. They are so dangerously good. I told myself I was only going to have a handful a day, but I ended up eating half the container while watching that new baking show on Netflix. Have you seen it? The one where they have to make everything look like everyday objects? It is so crazy. Someone made a cake that looked exactly like a sewing machine, down to the little spool of thread. I don't even know how you cut into something like that. I'd feel bad destroying it. I tried to bake a cake for my husband's birthday once, just a regular chocolate one, and it completely sank in the middle. It looked like a crater. I tried to fill the hole with extra frosting, but... 

Wait, sorry, sitting still. Right. Yeah, sitting still is definitely a big problem for me. I'm always fidgeting or moving some part of my body, even when I'm trying not to.

But I always end up talking, or humming some song that's stuck in my head, or getting up to grab a glass of water, or fixing a pillow, or just... making enough noise that it stops being peaceful. 

My husband is so patient, though. He usually just puts his headphones on. He has those really nice noise-canceling ones, the Bose ones? I bought them for him for our anniversary last year. We went to this Italian restaurant to celebrate, and the pasta was incredible, but the waiter kept hovering, which was kind of annoying. I hate when they ask how the food is right when you have a huge bite in your mouth. And then the table next to us was so loud, I think it was a bachelorette party or something. They had these little plastic tiaras. I wore a tiara for my wedding, actually, but it was real crystals, not plastic. It kept snagging in my veil, though. My hairdresser used, like, fifty bobby pins to keep it in place, and I had a headache for two days afterward. 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, playing quietly. Yeah, no, quiet just isn't really my thing, I guess. I just can't seem to settle down like that.

patient.answer:
I honestly don't know. I'm not really sure how to tell the difference between the two, to be honest. I actually tried looking that up on my iPad the other day to see if I could figure it out, but my iPad screen has this huge crack right down the middle. I dropped it in the driveway last week because I was trying to carry all the groceries inside in one trip. I absolutely refuse to make two trips. We use those heavy canvas bags from Trader Joe's, you know? Have you seen those little mini tote bags they came out with recently? People were literally fighting over them in the stores. My niece showed me a video of it on her phone. She's sixteen and she just got her learner's permit, which is terrifying. My sister let me ride in the back seat with them last weekend, and I swear I was pressing my foot on an imaginary brake pedal the entire time. She almost hit a mailbox. It was one of those really fancy brick mailboxes, too, the ones that look like a miniature house? If she had hit that, it would have completely totaled my sister's Honda. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking? Inattention or hyperactivity? Yeah, I really don't know. They just kind of feel like a big blur to me, so I couldn't really say if one is the main issue over the other.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely. Following through is... it's a real struggle. Like, if my husband asks me to handle a few things in order, you know? Like, "Can you call the plumber, update the calendar, and send that form?" I'll do the first part, I'll call the plumber, but then I'll just drift into something else before the rest is finished. 

Speaking of the plumber, he came over last week to fix the sink in the guest bathroom. It had been dripping for months, just this constant *drip, drip, drip*. It was driving me insane. But he was this really nice older guy, and he brought his dog with him! He just left him in the truck, but I went out and pet him. It was a golden retriever mix, I think. I love golden retrievers. We had one growing up named Buster, and he used to steal my dad's socks and hide them under the sofa. My dad would get so mad because he only wore those really specific wool socks from L.L. Bean. They're super warm, though. I should probably buy a pair before winter hits. The winters here have been getting so cold lately. Last year, our heating bill was absolutely ridiculous. I tried to tell my husband we need to weather-strip the windows, but... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, following through. Yeah, I definitely have a hard time finishing a list of things. I just get sidetracked so easily.

patient.answer:
I mean, I think the fidgeting is probably worse? Or at least, it's more obvious to other people. Like, even when I'm trying really, really hard to look composed, I just can't stop moving. If we're at a family dinner or, like, a church meeting, I'm always twisting my wedding ring around my finger, or my foot is just bouncing under the table, or I'm shifting in my chair. 

Speaking of my wedding ring, I actually need to get it resized. My knuckles have gotten kind of swollen lately, I don't know why. Maybe I'm eating too much salt? I did buy those sea salt caramel pretzels from Costco last week, the ones in the huge tub. They are so dangerously good. I told myself I was only going to have a handful a day, but I ended up eating half the container while watching that new baking show on Netflix. Have you seen it? The one where they have to make everything look like everyday objects? It is so crazy. Someone made a cake that looked exactly like a sewing machine, down to the little spool of thread. I don't even know how you cut into something like that. I'd feel bad destroying it. I tried to bake a cake for my husband's birthday once, just a regular chocolate one, and it completely sank in the middle. It looked like a crater. I tried to fill the hole with extra frosting, but... 

Wait, sorry, sitting still. Right. Yeah, sitting still is definitely a big problem for me. I'm always fidgeting or moving some part of my body, even when I'm trying not to.
